subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should OpenClaw replace the reusable inbound system-tag sanitizer with marker/envelope boundaries plus queued-event-only `System:` neutralization for all current prompt-bound external text?
rationale: This is an intentional security-contract and upgrade-policy choice, not a mechanical correctness question: the branch narrows a general defense while preserving one identified rendering invariant.

options.title: Approve the scoped boundary model
options.body: Confirm the complete external-text-path audit and accept marker/envelope boundaries with queue-level line neutralization as the canonical security contract.

options.title: Retain a shared sanitizer
options.body: Keep a narrowly specified reusable sanitizer for any prompt-bound external text path that is not proven to be structurally isolated.

options.title: Split the migration from the policy change
options.body: Land the marker and compatibility migration separately, then resolve sanitizer removal through a focused security decision.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped boundary model
recommendation.body: Confirm the complete external-text-path audit and accept marker/envelope boundaries with queue-level line neutralization as the canonical security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the same inbound-context prompt surface provides the closest available adjacent ownership signal for the security-contract choice.
